Lessons.Title: Multiplication Equations
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: represent and interpret multiplication equations from equal groups, pictures and tape diagrams; write a full equation with factors, equality and product (2021 IM first edition Grade 3 Unit 1 Lesson 13; CCSS 3.OA.A.1, 3.OA.A.3). The text and examples below are independently authored.
Warm-up: Represent three groups of 5 as a first-party drawing; distinguish 3×5, 2×5=10 and 7+8=15. Various WODB answers valid with explanation.
Activity 1 tasks: Nine original situations: 2 tapes of 10; 5 sock pairs; 8 pairs of 2 pictured; 6 hands of 5; 3 dot cubes of 5; 4 tape fives; 5 arrays of ten; 4 tape twos; 4 boxes of ten.

Activity 2 tasks: Seven originals: six pairs of socks (12); seven groups of two (14); seven notebook sections of ten (70); nine groups of two (18); six parts of ten (60); four orange bags of five (20); eight groups of five (40).
Lesson synthesis: Compare 3×5 and 3×5=15; factor and product language; 2021 source explicitly permits either factor order, with explanation; MLR7 peer comparison.
Independent Cool-down: Edulytics first-party 3 groups of 5 counters, full equation needed; original gated publisher Cool-down is not claimed copied.

Lesson timing: 10-minute Which One Doesn't Belong warm-up, 20-minute multiplication equation match, 15-minute write-equations activity, 10-minute synthesis and separate 5-minute Edulytics equivalent Cool-down.

Source evidence: 11 original publisher SVG assets were retrieved separately for authoring review only and are not embedded or reproduced. The third previously unlabelled figure contains eight outlined pairs of blue dots (16 total); the eighth shows a 4-part tape with 2 in each part (8 total). All 16 student tasks are present separately in the first-party Grade3 companion.

KeyConcepts.Title: Expression or equation
KeyConcepts.Definition: An expression names factors and an operation; an equation asserts a true equality.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A full equation has both factors, an equals sign and the correct product.
KeyConcepts.Example: 3 × 5 is an expression; 3 × 5 = 15 is an equation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal groups
KeyConcepts.Definition: An equal-groups representation has the same quantity in each group.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Count groups and objects per group and multiply.

KeyConcepts.Title: Tapes and dot arrays
KeyConcepts.Definition: Segmented tapes and arrays show multiplication geometrically.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve both factor meanings and the original total.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factor ordering
KeyConcepts.Definition: Reversing two whole-number multiplication factors preserves their product.
KeyConcepts.Rule: This 2021 source accepts either order; the student must still explain how the factors relate to the source model.
KeyConcepts.Example: 5 × 2 = 10 and 2 × 5 = 10 are both true for five sock pairs.

WorkedExamples.Title: Warm-up reasoning
WorkedExamples.Question: Which of a 3×5 dot drawing, 3×5, 2×5=10, and 7+8=15 does not belong?
WorkedExamples.Method: Compare representation, operation and equals sign; many reasoned choices possible.
Steps: Classify the drawing as a picture.
Explain one or more defensible differences to a partner.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Multiple choices may be supported, depending on the student's stated property.
WorkedExamples.Check: Human teacher review; no unique numeric pass.

WorkedExamples.Title: Previously unlabelled source dot drawing
WorkedExamples.Question: The 2021 source third activity picture shows eight distinct two-dot groups: write its equation.
WorkedExamples.Method: Count grouped dots; use complete equality.
Steps: Count eight outlined pairs across two rows.
Notice each outlined pair contains two colored dots.
Compute eight times two to find sixteen.
WorkedExamples.Check: Sixteen colored dots, verified against downloaded original SVG geometry.

WorkedExamples.Title: Previously unlabelled source tape
WorkedExamples.Question: The eighth source picture is divided into four equal sections with a two in each. Write the equation.
WorkedExamples.Method: Translate equal-length tape parts into equal groups.
Steps: Read the value two in each section.
Write a full multiplication equation with 4 and 2.
WorkedExamples.Check: Four partitions and total 8 were extracted from original first-edition SVG.

WorkedExamples.Title: Write original source equations
WorkedExamples.Question: Write equations for six sock pairs, seven twos, seven tens, nine twos, six tens, four bags of five, eight fives.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain the two factors and their product for each mathematical context.
Steps: Write 8 × 5 = 40; justify all models with a partner.
WorkedExamples.Check: Sixteen original source subtasks have separate model/equation fields with teacher justification.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Writing only a product, not an equation.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks for an equation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Write two factors, ×, =, and the correct product.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Teacher source says group-first is not required.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Both orders are valid for this lesson; review reasoning.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating unlabeled publisher drawings as unavailable when SVG geometry is accessible.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original figures are mathematical evidence even without alt text.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use the verified 8×2=16 and 4×2=8 source geometries; never copy original image assets.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating a unique-choice warm-up as numeric.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Which One Doesn't Belong admits different defensible properties.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Assign teacher review to all warm-up reasoning.

SummaryPoints: All nine source equation matches and all seven write-equation tasks are individually mapped.
Original two missing-alt drawings are mathematically identified as eight pairs (16) and four groups of two (8).
Original teacher language supports both factor orders; machine grading is restricted to correct full equations and defers reasoning to a teacher.
Independent Cool-down is equivalent in multiplication-equation skill, not a publisher copy.
Publisher PDF fetch failed 404 but original 2021 lesson HTML and all original figure SVG source files were directly reviewed; no publisher SVG reuse.
Stage D tests/builds/runtime publishing and academic approval remain explicitly unexecuted.
